_example_note: SIMULATED EXAMPLE. Generated by feeding synthetic 200 Hz lines (with a micros() wrap, 4 lost samples, a duplicate, an out-of-order sample, a corrupt line and a Zero) through the real app parser. NOT a hardware recording: data_source says 'hardware' only because the lines arrived through the USB code path.
calibration_source: Final Test Results.xlsx, sheet PVC (linear); S1-S7test results.xlsx (curve model)
device_time_source: MCU micros() read just before the 7-channel ADC burst of the sample (acquisition start); dev_us = unwrapped uint32 count, dev_ms = dev_us / 1000
sample_sequence_definition: sample_seq = uint32 counter kept by the MCU, +1 per acquisition cycle (first sample after boot = 0, wraps after 2^32 samples = 248 days at 200 Hz); a jump > 1 = missing samples, 0 = duplicate, backwards = out of order or MCU restart. Rows are written in arrival order. missing_samples adds (jump - 1) for every forward jump relative to the highest sequence number received so far; a late (out-of-order) sample is counted as out_of_order and does not reduce missing_samples. BLE v1 (firmware <= 1.3): the 16-bit counter unwrapped by the app.

time_columns.t_ms: host time since recording start, mapped from the device clock when one exists (app internal timebase, 3 decimals)
time_columns.dev_ms: device time in ms (blank when no device time exists)
time_columns.host_rx_utc_ms: host receive time, Unix UTC ms (USB: time the line was parsed; BLE v2: all 4 samples of a notification share it); for communication diagnostics, not the sampling clock

masks.sensor_valid_mask: bit i = 1 when sensor i delivered a finite mV > 0 (a disconnected pin cannot be detected by the hardware); bit0 S1, bit1 S4, bit2 S6, bit3 S11, bit4 S13, bit5 S10, bit6 S14
masks.saturation_mask: bit i = 1 when mV >= 3250 (ADC / amplifier limit, force is then a lower bound), same bit order

fz_definition: Fz_N = sum of the 7 S*_N, unscaled (no area or body-weight scaling). Fz_BW_N = Fz_N x body-weight factor, blank when no factor was set
negative_values_policy: N = max(0, F - tare_N): negative forces are clamped to 0 N; mV is exported as received
acquisition_note: ADC: 12 bit, 11 dB attenuation, analogReadMilliVolts, 8 reads averaged per channel per sample (firmware OVERSAMPLE); no other filtering or resampling is applied in the app or in the export

coordinates.cop_origin_definition: Middle of the insole outline bounding box (90.73 x 272.01 mm): 45.365 mm from the outline's left edge and 136.005 mm from its heel end. This is the origin the app itself uses (centred origin, in use since app 1.4 on 2026-11-12). CSV files recorded before that used the CAD corner origin instead.
coordinates.cop_x_axis_definition: Mediolateral (ML), along the horizontal axis of the insole drawing
coordinates.cop_x_positive_direction: Toward the right of the insole drawing (top view, toes up): MEDIAL (big-toe side) for the LEFT insole; for the RIGHT insole, which is the mirror image, LATERAL

canonical_cad_frame.name: insole_cad_corner_mm
canonical_cad_frame.origin: Bottom-left corner of the insole outline bounding box (heel end, left edge, drawing viewed from above with toes up)
canonical_cad_frame.x_axis: ML, + toward the right of the drawing

coordinates.transform_note: [x_cad, y_cad, 1]^T = M x [COPx_mm, COPy_mm, 1]^T. The sensor positions in metadata are given in both frames.
coordinates.cop_formula: COP = sum(r_i * N_i) / sum(N_i) over the 7 sensors, N_i = calibrated force of sensor i (S*_N, after tare and clamping at 0 N), r_i = sensor position
coordinates.cop_valid_rule: COPx_mm / COPy_mm are left blank when Fz_N <= 10 N (no contact); they are never written as (0, 0)

L.device_time_source: MCU micros() read just before the 7-channel ADC burst of the sample (acquisition start); dev_us = unwrapped uint32 count, dev_ms = dev_us / 1000

configuration_policy: Calibration, tare/baseline, mapping and CoP geometry are snapshotted at the foot's first recorded sample (feet[*].sensors). Any later change is listed in events (ZERO, TARE_CHANGE, CALIBRATION_CHANGE) with old and new values; the snapshot is never overwritten.
